intent: To demonstrate that combining estate, corporate, and property taxes results in a much heavier tax burden for the wealthiest individuals.

requirements.question: Should the video explicitly present 11.7% as the Richest group's combined total from the two visible segments?
Should the video state the Richest-vs-Poorest gap explicitly rather than only showing the two bars?
Should the video show the full ordered progression of corporate/property taxes, or only the Richest and Poorest endpoints?
Should the video explicitly identify estate taxes as a separate stacked component for the Richest and 10th groups?

units.claim: For the Richest group, combining corporate/property taxes (10.9%) with estate taxes (0.8%) produces a total tax burden of 11.7%.
accept: The Richest group's combined tax burden is 11.7%.
Corporate and property taxes plus estate taxes total 11.7% for the Richest.
For the Richest, 10.9% corporate/property and 0.8% estate stack to 11.7%.
units.evidence: Richest bar must show a stacked total of 11.7, with visible segments 10.9 and 0.8 or a label for 11.7.

units.claim: The Richest group's total tax burden (11.7%) is far heavier than the Poorest group's (1.4%), a gap of 10.3 percentage points and roughly 8.4 times the Poorest rate.
accept: Richest total is 10.3 percentage points above Poorest (11.7% vs 1.4%).
The Richest burden is about 8.4 times the Poorest burden.
The combined burden is far heavier for the Richest than for the Poorest (11.7% vs 1.4%).
units.evidence: Chart must allow direct comparison of Richest total (11.7) and Poorest total (1.4) on the same scale.

units.claim: Corporate and property taxes increase monotonically across wealth groups from 1.4% for the Poorest to 10.9% for the Richest, with the top two groups much higher than lower groups (10th at 9.6%, Richest at 10.9%).
accept: Corporate and property tax rates rise with wealth, from 1.4% for the Poorest to 10.9% for the Richest.
The top two groups have the highest corporate/property tax segments (10th: 9.6%; Richest: 10.9%).
The burden increases stepwise across the wealth groups, reaching 10.9% for the Richest.
units.evidence: Bars must be ordered by wealth group and show the upward progression of the corporate/property tax segment.

units.claim: Estate taxes are a separate component for the top groups: 0.3 percentage points for the 10th group and 0.8 percentage points for the Richest.
accept: Estate taxes add 0.3 points for the 10th group and 0.8 points for the Richest.
The estate-tax segment is 0.8% for the Richest and 0.3% for the 10th group.
Estate taxes appear as the smaller stacked segment for the top two groups.
units.evidence: Stacked bars for 10th and Richest must include a distinct estate-tax segment (0.3 and 0.8) separate from corporate/property taxes.

optional_valid: The 10th group's combined total is 9.9% (9.6 corporate/property + 0.3 estate).
The Richest corporate/property tax segment alone is 10.9%, already higher than every lower group's corporate/property tax value.
Exact ratio Richest total to Poorest total is about 8.36x, if more precision is desired than 8.4x.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
